memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The whole Israelite community set out from the Desert of Sin, traveling from
place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no
water for the people to drink." - Ex 17:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read the two halves of this verse together, because the whole chapter turns on
them.

They travelled "as the LORD commanded." And when they arrived, "there was no
water."

Both statements are true at once. They were exactly where God told them to be,
and there was nothing to drink. God did not misdirect them. He did not lose track
of their needs. He led them to a place with no water.

This is the second time Exodus has done this to us. At Marah the water was
bitter; here there is none at all. The Bible seems determined that we should not
draw the easy conclusion that obedience guarantees comfort.

That conclusion is common and it does real damage. When people are taught that
following God means smooth circumstances, then hardship becomes evidence of
failure, and they start hunting for the sin that caused it. Sometimes hardship
does follow from our choices. Often it does not.

Jesus was in the centre of His Father's will in Gethsemane, and it was the
hardest night of His life.

Being in a hard place is not proof that you have wandered. Sometimes it is proof
that you have followed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you assume difficulty means you have gone wrong somewhere?
2. Can you hold obedience and hardship together without panicking?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when I obey You and still find myself in a dry place, help me not to
doubt Your leading. Thank You that You know exactly where I am. Amen.
